senses.en: A very small statue.

ex.en: A bronze statuette of a horse was found.
ex.zh: 出土了一尊青铜小马像。

senses.en: An object worn to protect against evil.

ex.en: She wore an amulet for luck.
ex.zh: 她戴着护身符求好运。

senses.en: An object believed to have magic power.

ex.en: The ring was a family talisman.
ex.zh: 这枚戒指是家族的护身符。

senses.en: To strongly disapprove of something or deeply regret it

ex.en: Our neighbours deplore the dumping of rubbish beside the river.
ex.zh: 邻居们强烈谴责在河边倾倒垃圾的行为。

ex.en: Many educators deplore funding cuts that limit access to music and art lessons in public schools.
ex.zh: 许多教育工作者强烈反对削减经费，因为这限制了公立学校学生接受音乐和美术教育的机会。

col: deplore the lack of｜对缺乏……深感遗憾
deplore the decision｜强烈反对该决定
tip: 正式及物动词，后直接接所谴责或痛惜的事。

senses.en: An animal or object that is a symbol of a group.

ex.en: The eagle was the clan's totem.
ex.zh: 鹰是这个氏族的图腾。

senses.en: A model or statue of a person.

ex.en: Protesters burned an effigy of the king.
ex.zh: 抗议者焚烧了国王的模拟像。

senses.en: Offered to a god as a gift or promise.

ex.en: Votive offerings were left at the shrine.
ex.zh: 神龛前留有还愿供品。

senses.en: An underground room beneath a church, often used for burials.

ex.en: Kings were buried in the crypt.
ex.zh: 国王们葬在地下墓室里。

senses.en: A stone coffin.

ex.en: The pharaoh's sarcophagus was carved from granite.
ex.zh: 法老的石棺由花岗岩雕成。

senses.en: A rigid support that keeps an injured body part still.
To support an injured body part with a splint.

ex.en: The nurse fitted a splint to my injured finger.
ex.zh: 护士给我受伤的手指装上了夹板。

ex.en: Using a splint to stabilise an injured limb can prevent further damage while patients await medical treatment.
ex.zh: 在患者等待医疗救治时，用夹板固定受伤的肢体可以防止进一步损伤。

tip: 指固定伤处的夹板；不同于石膏固定用的cast。

senses.en: A body preserved by drying, especially in ancient Egypt.

ex.en: The mummy was wrapped in linen.
ex.zh: 木乃伊用亚麻布包裹着。

senses.en: The process of preserving a dead body by drying it.

ex.en: Mummification took about seventy days.
ex.zh: 制作木乃伊大约需要七十天。

senses.en: Treating a dead body with chemicals to preserve it.

ex.en: Egyptian embalming used salt and resin.
ex.zh: 埃及的防腐处理使用盐和树脂。

senses.en: Burning a dead body to ashes.

ex.en: Cremation was common in ancient Rome.
ex.zh: 火葬在古罗马很普遍。

senses.en: A tall vase, often used to hold the ashes of the dead.

ex.en: Ashes were placed in a clay urn.
ex.zh: 骨灰被放进一个陶瓮里。

senses.en: soldiers trained to fight on foot

ex.en: The infantry marched past our village early this morning.
ex.zh: 今天一大早，步兵部队行军经过了我们的村庄。

ex.en: Although military technology has changed considerably, infantry still play an important role in many countries' defence forces.
ex.zh: 尽管军事技术发生了巨大变化，步兵在许多国家的国防力量中仍发挥着重要作用。

tip: 集合名词，指步兵整体，不用an infantry指一个人。

senses.en: A container or room for the bones of the dead.

ex.en: The ossuary held hundreds of skulls.
ex.zh: 藏骨堂里有数百个头骨。

senses.en: An underground cemetery of tunnels.

ex.en: Early Christians were buried in the catacombs of Rome.
ex.zh: 早期基督徒葬在罗马的地下墓穴中。

senses.en: A large ancient cemetery.

ex.en: Giza is a vast necropolis of pyramids.
ex.zh: 吉萨是一片巨大的金字塔墓地。

senses.en: An ancient burial mound; a small cart.

ex.en: Bronze Age chiefs were buried in barrows.
ex.zh: 青铜时代的首领葬在古坟里。

senses.en: An ancient burial mound.

ex.en: The tumulus covers a stone chamber.
ex.zh: 坟丘下面是一个石室。

senses.en: A round bacterium forming clusters, sometimes causing infections.

ex.en: The laboratory found staphylococcus in the skin sample.
ex.zh: 实验室在皮肤样本中发现了葡萄球菌。

ex.en: Some strains of staphylococcus resist common antibiotics, making hospital infections more difficult to treat.
ex.zh: 某些葡萄球菌菌株对常用抗生素具有耐药性，使医院感染更难治疗。

col: strains of staphylococcus｜葡萄球菌菌株
antibiotic-resistant staphylococcus｜耐抗生素葡萄球菌

senses.en: A pile of stones built as a marker or memorial.

ex.en: Hikers added a stone to the cairn.
ex.zh: 徒步者往石堆上添了一块石头。

senses.en: An ancient tomb of large upright stones with a flat stone on top.

ex.en: The dolmen is over 5,000 years old.
ex.zh: 这座石棚墓有五千多年历史。

senses.en: A very large stone used in ancient monuments.

ex.en: Builders moved megaliths without wheels.
ex.zh: 建造者在没有轮子的情况下搬运巨石。

senses.en: A single great block of stone; a large unchanging organization.

ex.en: A monolith stands alone on the hill.
ex.zh: 一块巨石孤零零地矗立在山上。

senses.en: A tall upright prehistoric stone.

ex.en: Rows of menhirs stretch across the field.
ex.zh: 一排排糙石巨柱横贯田野。

senses.en: to appoint someone to act or perform a task for you

ex.en: The manager deputed her assistant to attend the meeting.
ex.zh: 经理委派她的助理去参加会议。

ex.en: Local authorities may depute trained officers to inspect buildings and ensure compliance with safety regulations.
ex.zh: 地方政府可以委派受过培训的官员检查建筑，确保其符合安全规定。

col: depute someone to do something｜委派某人做某事
tip: 正式用词，常用depute sb to do sth。

senses.en: A prehistoric circular earthwork, often with standing stones.

ex.en: The henge was aligned with the summer sunrise.
ex.zh: 这座环状列石与夏至日出方向对齐。

senses.en: A picture carved into rock.

ex.en: Petroglyphs show hunters and deer.
ex.zh: 岩刻上画着猎人和鹿。

senses.en: A picture representing a word or idea; a painting on rock.

ex.en: Early writing began with pictographs.
ex.zh: 早期文字始于象形图。

senses.en: A carved symbol or character.

ex.en: Mayan glyphs record dates and kings.
ex.zh: 玛雅象形符号记载了日期和国王。

senses.en: A picture symbol used in ancient Egyptian writing.

ex.en: Each hieroglyph could stand for a sound or idea.
ex.zh: 每个象形文字可以代表一个音或一个概念。

senses.en: to surround or cover something, especially with smoke or mist

ex.en: Thin wisps of steam wreathed her face above the bowl.
ex.zh: 碗里升起的缕缕蒸汽缭绕在她脸庞周围。

ex.en: Smoke from nearby factories can wreathe residential buildings, highlighting the need for stricter industrial emission controls.
ex.zh: 附近工厂排出的烟雾可能笼罩住宅楼，凸显加强工业排放管控的必要性。

col: be wreathed in smoke｜被烟雾笼罩
mist wreathes the hills｜薄雾环绕山丘
a face wreathed in smiles｜满面笑容

senses.en: Written in hieroglyphs.

ex.en: Hieroglyphic texts cover the temple walls.
ex.zh: 神庙墙壁上满是象形文字。

senses.en: An ancient writing system of wedge-shaped marks.

ex.en: Cuneiform was pressed into clay tablets.
ex.zh: 楔形文字被压印在泥板上。

senses.en: The study of ancient inscriptions.

ex.en: Epigraphy helped date the monument.
ex.zh: 铭文学帮助确定了纪念碑的年代。

senses.en: A plant, or the paper made from it in ancient Egypt.

ex.en: The text was written on papyrus.
ex.zh: 这段文字写在纸莎草纸上。

senses.en: Writing material made from animal skin.

ex.en: Medieval books were written on parchment.
ex.zh: 中世纪书籍写在羊皮纸上。

senses.en: a layer of rock or soil that holds underground water

ex.en: The town gets its water from a deep aquifer.
ex.zh: 这个镇的用水来自一个很深的含水层。

ex.en: When farmers pump water from an aquifer faster than rain can refill it, the water table drops and wells eventually run dry.
ex.zh: 当农民抽取含水层的水比降雨补给更快时，地下水位就会下降，水井最终会干涸。

tip: aqua-（水）+ -fer（携带）。托福地科、环境话题高频。

senses.en: An ancient handwritten book with pages.

ex.en: The codex replaced the scroll.
ex.zh: 古抄本取代了卷轴。

senses.en: Working out the meaning of a code or ancient script.

ex.en: The decipherment of hieroglyphs took decades.
ex.zh: 破译象形文字花了几十年。

senses.en: Relating to layers of soil or rock.

ex.en: Stratigraphic evidence placed the hearth below the wall.
ex.zh: 地层证据表明火塘在墙的下面。

senses.en: A radioactive form of carbon used to date ancient objects.

ex.en: Radiocarbon dating showed the bones were 10,000 years old.
ex.zh: 放射性碳测年显示这些骨头有一万年历史。

senses.en: Light released when a material is heated, used to date pottery.

ex.en: Thermoluminescence dated the pottery.
ex.zh: 热释光测出了陶器的年代。

senses.en: A spinning mass of fluid drawing things towards its centre
A situation that pulls people into increasing confusion or difficulty

ex.en: Leaves spun in a vortex beside the riverbank.
ex.zh: 树叶在河岸旁的旋涡中打转。

ex.en: Without access to affordable credit, some households become trapped in a vortex of debt and financial insecurity.
ex.zh: 如果无法获得利率可负担的贷款，一些家庭就会陷入债务与财务不稳定的旋涡。

col: a vortex of debt｜债务旋涡
be sucked into a vortex｜被卷入旋涡
tip: 复数可用vortices或vortexes；也可比喻困境。

senses.en: Classifying things by type.

ex.en: Pottery typology helps date sites.
ex.zh: 陶器类型学有助于确定遗址年代。

senses.en: Placing objects in order by changes in their style.

ex.en: Seriation ordered the graves by their pottery.
ex.zh: 排序法根据陶器给墓葬排了先后。

senses.en: A group of objects found together.

ex.en: The tool assemblage included scrapers and blades.
ex.zh: 这组工具包括刮削器和刀片。

senses.en: The place of origin or history of ownership of an object.

ex.en: The museum checked the vase's provenance.
ex.zh: 博物馆核查了这只花瓶的来源。

senses.en: A small hand tool with a flat blade.

ex.en: Archaeologists dig slowly with trowels.
ex.zh: 考古学家用小铲慢慢挖掘。

senses.en: to prevent something or make it impossible

ex.en: The heavy rain precluded our planned picnic by the lake.
ex.zh: 大雨让我们原定的湖边野餐无法进行。

ex.en: High tuition fees may preclude students from disadvantaged backgrounds from accessing higher education without financial support.
ex.zh: 高昂的学费可能使弱势家庭的学生在没有经济资助的情况下无法接受高等教育。

col: preclude someone from doing something｜使某人无法做某事
preclude further discussion｜使进一步讨论无法进行
tip: 正式用词；可用preclude sb from doing sth。

senses.en: A tool with a mesh for separating fine from coarse material.

ex.en: Soil was passed through a sieve to find beads.
ex.zh: 土壤过筛以寻找珠子。

senses.en: An early survey to gather information.

ex.en: An aerial reconnaissance spotted the buried walls.
ex.zh: 航空勘察发现了埋藏的墙基。

senses.en: A method of mapping using laser pulses.

ex.en: Lidar revealed lost Maya cities under the jungle.
ex.zh: 激光雷达揭示了丛林下失落的玛雅城市。

senses.en: Measuring magnetic fields to find buried features.

ex.en: Magnetometry located ancient kilns.
ex.zh: 磁力测量找到了古代窑址。

senses.en: An exact copy of something.

ex.en: The museum displays a replica of the crown.
ex.zh: 博物馆展出了王冠的复制品。

senses.en: Produced or expressed in very large amounts

ex.en: He offered profuse apologies for spilling my tea.
ex.zh: 他打翻了我的茶，连声道歉。

ex.en: Profuse sweating during outdoor exercise can increase fluid loss, making regular water intake particularly important.
ex.zh: 户外运动时大量出汗会增加水分流失，因此定期补水尤为重要。

tip: 常修饰出汗、道歉或感谢，强调量大或反复。

senses.en: Building something again, or showing how it once was.

ex.en: A reconstruction shows the village as it looked.
ex.zh: 复原图展示了村庄当年的样子。

senses.en: A person in charge of a museum collection.

ex.en: The curator chose the objects for the exhibit.
ex.zh: 策展人为展览挑选了展品。

senses.en: Relating to the work of a curator.

ex.en: The curatorial team wrote the labels.
ex.zh: 策展团队撰写了说明牌。

senses.en: A member of the family including humans and great apes.

ex.en: Hominid fossils were found in the gorge.
ex.zh: 在峡谷中发现了人科动物化石。

senses.en: A member of the group including humans and their extinct close relatives.

ex.en: Lucy is a famous early hominin.
ex.zh: 露西是著名的早期人族成员。

senses.en: To make someone annoyed, worried, or frustrated.

ex.en: The constant dripping from the tap began to vex him.
ex.zh: 水龙头不停滴水，开始让他心烦。

ex.en: Disagreements over how to fund public transport continue to vex policymakers in many growing cities.
ex.zh: 在许多不断发展的城市，公共交通资金来源的分歧仍困扰着政策制定者。

col: be vexed by delays｜因延误而烦恼
tip: 较正式的及物动词，日常多用annoy。

senses.en: An early human relative that walked upright.

ex.en: Australopithecus lived in Africa millions of years ago.
ex.zh: 南方古猿数百万年前生活在非洲。

senses.en: An extinct human species that lived in Europe and Asia.

ex.en: Neanderthals buried their dead.
ex.zh: 尼安德特人会埋葬死者。

senses.en: Walking on two legs.

ex.en: Bipedalism freed early humans' hands.
ex.zh: 两足行走解放了早期人类的双手。

senses.en: Able to be placed against the other fingers.

ex.en: Primates have opposable thumbs.
ex.zh: 灵长类动物有可对握的拇指。

senses.en: The part of the skull that holds the brain.

ex.en: The cranium was larger than expected.
ex.zh: 这块颅骨比预想的大。

senses.en: The lower jawbone.

ex.en: A mandible with teeth was found.
ex.zh: 发现了一块带牙的下颌骨。

senses.en: A small detail or distinction requiring careful understanding
A small convention of polite social behaviour

ex.en: I am still learning the niceties of formal dining.
ex.zh: 我还在学习正式用餐的礼仪细节。

ex.en: Understanding the niceties of legal language is essential when translating international agreements that affect trade and environmental protection.
ex.zh: 翻译涉及贸易和环境保护的国际协议时，理解法律语言的细微差别至关重要。

col: legal niceties｜法律上的细微区别
tip: 多用复数 niceties，勿直接理解为“美好”。

senses.en: The thigh bone.

ex.en: The femur showed the person walked upright.
ex.zh: 股骨显示此人直立行走。

senses.en: The study of bones.

ex.en: Osteology reveals age and diet.
ex.zh: 骨学能揭示年龄和饮食。

senses.en: The study of human remains from archaeological sites.

ex.en: Bioarchaeology shows how ancient people lived.
ex.zh: 生物考古学揭示古人如何生活。

senses.en: The study of human evolution through fossils.

ex.en: Paleoanthropology traces our ancestors.
ex.zh: 古人类学追溯我们的祖先。

senses.en: The detailed study of a particular culture.

ex.en: Her ethnography describes village life.
ex.zh: 她的民族志描述了乡村生活。

senses.en: to distort something good or proper for harmful purposes

ex.en: The coach perverted fair competition by secretly changing the rules.
ex.zh: 教练暗中修改规则，破坏了公平竞争。

ex.en: Political pressure can pervert scientific research when funding depends on producing results that support existing policies.
ex.zh: 当资助取决于研究结果是否支持现行政策时，政治压力可能使科研偏离正轨。

col: pervert the course of justice｜妨碍司法公正
tip: 动词重音在后；名词重音在前且常含贬义。

senses.en: A person who studies and describes cultures.

ex.en: The ethnographer recorded local songs.
ex.zh: 这位民族志学者记录了当地歌曲。

senses.en: Relating to the study of cultures.

ex.en: Ethnographic fieldwork takes many months.
ex.zh: 民族志田野调查需要好几个月。

senses.en: The comparative study of cultures.

ex.en: Ethnology compares customs across societies.
ex.zh: 民族学比较不同社会的习俗。

senses.en: Family relationship.

ex.en: Kinship ties organize village life.
ex.zh: 亲属关系组织着乡村生活。

senses.en: A society ruled by a chief.

ex.en: Chiefdoms were larger than tribes.
ex.zh: 酋邦比部落规模更大。

senses.en: The theft of small amounts or items, especially from workplaces.

ex.en: The shop now locks its stockroom to prevent pilferage.
ex.zh: 这家商店现在把库房锁起来，以防东西被顺手偷走。

ex.en: Retailers can reduce losses from pilferage by improving stock monitoring and providing secure storage for valuable goods.
ex.zh: 零售商可以通过加强库存监控并为贵重商品提供安全储存空间，减少小额失窃造成的损失。

col: losses from pilferage｜小额失窃造成的损失
tip: pilferage是不可数名词，不是动词；动词为pilfer。

senses.en: A way of life based on raising livestock.

ex.en: Pastoralism suits dry grasslands.
ex.zh: 畜牧生活适合干旱草原。

senses.en: A person who looks after a herd of animals.

ex.en: Herders move their goats to new pastures.
ex.zh: 牧人把山羊赶到新的牧场。

senses.en: A person who lives by hunting animals and gathering wild plants.

ex.en: Humans were hunter-gatherers for most of history.
ex.zh: 在历史的大部分时间里，人类是狩猎采集者。

senses.en: A person or animal that searches for food.

ex.en: Foragers knew hundreds of edible plants.
ex.zh: 采集者认识数百种可食用植物。

senses.en: Staying in one place; involving much sitting.

ex.en: Farming led to sedentary villages.
ex.zh: 农业催生了定居的村落。

senses.en: showing strength and energy traditionally associated with men

ex.en: The sculpture portrays a virile athlete lifting a discus.
ex.zh: 这座雕塑刻画了一位举起铁饼、充满阳刚之气的运动员。

ex.en: Advertisements often present a virile male ideal, which may reinforce narrow expectations about men's appearance and behaviour.
ex.zh: 广告常常展示阳刚的理想男性形象，这可能强化对男性外貌和行为的狭隘期待。

col: virile young man｜强健的年轻男子
tip: 不只是“男性的”；强调传统观念中的男性力量与活力。

senses.en: The practice of living in one place for a long time.

ex.en: Sedentism began before farming in some regions.
ex.zh: 在一些地区，定居早于农业出现。

senses.en: Taming animals or growing plants for human use.

ex.en: The domestication of wheat began 10,000 years ago.
ex.zh: 小麦的驯化始于一万年前。

senses.en: Relating to the Old Stone Age.

ex.en: Paleolithic people painted cave walls.
ex.zh: 旧石器时代的人在洞壁上作画。

senses.en: Relating to the Middle Stone Age.

ex.en: Mesolithic hunters used tiny stone blades.
ex.zh: 中石器时代的猎人使用细小石刃。

senses.en: Tracing family descent through the mother.

ex.en: In matrilineal societies, land passes to daughters.
ex.zh: 在母系社会中，土地传给女儿。

senses.en: a long, detailed piece of writing about a particular subject

ex.en: I found a dusty treatise on gardening upstairs.
ex.zh: 我在楼上找到了一本落满灰尘的园艺专著。

ex.en: The philosopher's treatise on education argues that practical experience should play a central role in learning.
ex.zh: 这位哲学家的教育论著主张，实践经验应在学习中发挥核心作用。

tip: 常用a treatise on，指系统详尽的专论而非短文。

senses.en: Tracing family descent through the father.

ex.en: Surnames are usually patrilineal.
ex.zh: 姓氏通常是父系传承的。

senses.en: Ruled or led by women.

ex.en: The elephant herd is matriarchal.
ex.zh: 象群是母系领导的。

senses.en: Ruled or controlled by men.

ex.en: The novel criticizes patriarchal society.
ex.zh: 这部小说批判了父权社会。

senses.en: A society in which women hold power.

ex.en: True matriarchies are rare.
ex.zh: 真正的母权社会很少见。

senses.en: A society in which men hold power.

ex.en: Feminists challenged patriarchy.
ex.zh: 女权主义者挑战父权制。
